papers.title: Detecting and Preventing Data Poisoning Attacks on AI Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the critical issue of data poisoning attacks on AI models, a growing concern in the ever-evolving landscape of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As advanced technology systems become increasingly prevalent across various sectors, the need for robust defence mechanisms against adversarial attacks becomes paramount. The study aims to develop and evaluate novel techniques for detecting and preventing data poisoning attacks, focusing on both theoretical frameworks and practical applications. Through a comprehensive literature review, experimental validation using the CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims datasets, and the development of innovative algorithms, this paper seeks to enhance the resilience of AI models against malicious data manipulation. The study explores various methods, including anomaly detection, robust optimization strategies, and ensemble learning, to identify and mitigate the effects of poisoned data during model training. Experimental results indicate that data poisoning significantly degrades model performance, reducing classification accuracy by up to 27 % in image recognition tasks (CIFAR-10) and 22 % in fraud detection models (Insurance Claims dataset). The proposed defence mechanisms, including statistical anomaly detection and adversarial training, successfully mitigated poisoning effects, improving model robustness and restoring accuracy levels by an average of $15-20 \%$. The findings further demonstrate that ensemble learning techniques provide an additional layer of resilience, reducing false positives and false negatives caused by adversarial data injections. The findings of this paper contribute to the broader understanding of adversarial machine learning and provide actionable insights for practitioners in industries facing emerging threats to AI-based systems. By addressing the challenges of data poisoning attacks, this study aims to improve the security and reliability of AI models, ultimately fostering greater trust in AI technologies across critical applications.

papers.title: Robust and Adaptive Dual-Defense Framework Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based recommendation systems are highly vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate user interactions to degrade model integrity. We hypothesize that combining an active robust loss with a passive GAN-based detection will significantly reduce poisoning impact in recommendation systems without sacrificing utility. We propose a robust and adaptive dual-defense framework: the active defense integrates a crafted loss function to mitigate poisoning effects while maintaining model performance. The passive defense employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based detection model to identify and filter poisoned data, enhancing detection accuracy and system security. The framework supports classical matrix factorization (MF) model and large language model (LLM)-based pipelines and scales to large datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets at varying poison rates show that our method outperforms representative defenses, consistently reducing attack success without sacrificing recommendation quality. The framework also admits a federated instantiation, where robust training and GAN-based detection run on clients and only privacy-preserving summaries are aggregated. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and adaptability of recommendation systems under data poisoning attacks.

papers.title: Towards Imperceptible and Robust Adversarial Example Attacks against Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Machine learning systems based on deep neural networks, being able to produce state-of-the-art results on various perception tasks, have gained mainstream adoption in many applications. However, they are shown to be vulnerable to adversarial example attack, which generates malicious output by adding slight perturbations to the input. Previous adversarial example crafting methods, however, use simple metrics to evaluate the distances between the original examples and the adversarial ones, which could be easily detected by human eyes. In addition, these attacks are often not robust due to the inevitable noises and deviation in the physical world. In this work, we present a new adversarial example attack crafting method, which takes the human perceptual system into consideration and maximizes the noise tolerance of the crafted adversarial example. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed technique.

papers.title: Robust Real-World Image Super-Resolution against Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: Recently deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved significant success in real-world image super-resolution (SR). However, adversarial image samples with quasi-imperceptible noises could threaten deep learning SR models. In this paper, we propose a robust deep learning framework for real-world SR that randomly erases potential adversarial noises in the frequency domain of input images or features. The rationale is that on the SR task clean images or features have a different pattern from the attacked ones in the frequency domain. Observing that existing adversarial attacks usually add high-frequency noises to input images, we introduce a novel random frequency mask module that blocks out high-frequency components possibly containing the harmful perturbations in a stochastic manner. Since the frequency masking may not only destroys the adversarial perturbations but also affects the sharp details in a clean image, we further develop an adversarial sample classifier based on the frequency domain of images to determine if applying the proposed mask module. Based on the above ideas, we devise a novel real-world image SR framework that combines the proposed frequency mask modules and the proposed adversarial classifier with an existing super-resolution backbone network. Experiments show that our proposed method is more insensitive to adversarial attacks and presents more stable SR results than existing models and defenses.

literature_themes.theme: Defensive Strategies Against Data Poisoning in AI Models
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers focuses on the detection and prevention of data poisoning attacks on AI models, particularly in the contexts of image recognition and recommendation systems. The studies propose various innovative techniques, including anomaly detection, robust optimization, and dual-defense frameworks that combine active and passive defenses, to enhance model resilience against malicious data manipulation. Experimental results indicate significant degradation in model performance due to data poisoning, highlighting the necessity for robust defense mechanisms.
literature_themes.limitations: The cluster lacks comprehensive exploration of the long-term effectiveness of proposed defenses and their adaptability across diverse datasets and attack scenarios. Additionally, one paper did not provide an abstract, limiting insights into its contributions.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster can support research gap identification by emphasizing the need for more generalized and scalable defense mechanisms against data poisoning, particularly in emerging AI applications and varied operational environments.

literature_themes.theme: Adversarial Robustness in Deep Learning Applications
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers focuses on enhancing the robustness of deep learning models against adversarial attacks, particularly in the context of image processing tasks. The first paper introduces a method for crafting adversarial examples that are imperceptible to humans while maximizing noise tolerance. The second paper presents a framework for image super-resolution that employs frequency domain techniques to mitigate the impact of adversarial noise, demonstrating a proactive approach to defend against such attacks.
literature_themes.limitations: Both papers highlight the challenge of balancing the removal of adversarial perturbations with the preservation of image quality. The methods proposed may still be susceptible to more sophisticated adversarial strategies and do not fully address the generalizability of the solutions across diverse datasets and real-world scenarios.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster identifies a critical research gap in developing robust defenses against adversarial attacks in deep learning, particularly in practical applications like image super-resolution. It underscores the need for further exploration of perceptual metrics and advanced noise mitigation techniques to enhance model resilience.

summary: The retrieved literature highlights two primary themes: defensive strategies against data poisoning and adversarial robustness in deep learning. The first theme emphasizes the need for comprehensive and scalable defense mechanisms against data poisoning, with proposed techniques showing promise but limited generalizability. The second theme identifies critical gaps in developing robust defenses against adversarial attacks, particularly in image processing, suggesting further exploration of perceptual metrics and advanced noise mitigation techniques to enhance model resilience.
literature_tension_graph: The existing literature presents a tension between the proposed dual-defense frameworks against data poisoning, which show promise in specific contexts like recommendation systems, and the lack of generalizability across diverse AI applications. This conflict is primarily evaluative, as the effectiveness of these defenses remains untested in broader operational environments. Additionally, while adversarial robustness techniques focus on crafting imperceptible attacks, they do not adequately address the preservation of image quality during defense, leading to unresolved questions about the trade-offs between robustness and performance. This suggests a research direction aimed at developing adaptable, scalable defense mechanisms that integrate insights from both data poisoning and adversarial robustness, potentially leading to more universally applicable solutions.
scholarly_positioning: Existing research has advanced defensive strategies against data poisoning and adversarial attacks, yet significant limitations persist regarding the generalizability and long-term effectiveness of these defenses across diverse datasets and operational contexts. While some studies propose innovative detection and dual-defense frameworks, they often lack comprehensive evaluation in real-world scenarios, leaving a gap in understanding their adaptability. Furthermore, the focus on specific applications, such as image recognition and recommendation systems, underscores an unresolved tension in developing universally applicable solutions. This proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by exploring scalable defense mechanisms that integrate insights from both data poisoning and adversarial robustness, thus contributing to the broader discourse on resilient AI systems.
research_scope: This study will focus on enhancing the robustness of deep learning models used in image recognition tasks against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The target population will include convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on benchmark datasets such as CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. The intervention will involve the development and evaluation of a dual-defense framework that integrates anomaly detection and frequency domain analysis over a study period of six months. The comparison group will consist of standard CNN architectures without the proposed defenses. Primary outcomes will include model accuracy and resilience to both data poisoning and adversarial perturbations, while secondary outcomes will assess the generalizability of the defense mechanisms across different datasets and attack scenarios.

Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of the dual-defense framework across diverse datasets and the interaction effects between the two defense mechanisms.

proposal: This research aims to enhance the robustness of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) against data poisoning and adversarial attacks in image recognition tasks by developing a novel dual-defense framework that integrates anomaly detection and frequency domain analysis. Current literature highlights a significant gap in the generalizability of dual-defense strategies across diverse AI applications, particularly in image recognition, where existing methods often fail to demonstrate adaptability and comprehensive evaluation in varied operational contexts. This study posits that effective anomaly detection identifies harmful patterns in training data (independent variable), while frequency domain analysis enhances feature representation (mediator), collectively leading to improved model resilience (dependent variable) against both data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The hypothesis is that the proposed dual-defense framework will significantly outperform standard CNN architectures in terms of model accuracy and resilience. Constructs will be operationalized through metrics such as model accuracy and robustness, with careful controls for dataset characteristics and attack types. The methodology will include rigorous ablation studies to isolate the contributions of each defense mechanism, ensuring robust baseline comparisons against standard CNNs. Validity will be maintained through monitoring confounding variables and employing statistical methods for evaluation. Expected contributions include advancing resilience theory by empirically demonstrating the effectiveness of integrated defense mechanisms, providing actionable guidelines for deploying robust AI systems, and addressing critical gaps in operational AI resilience. This research directly responds to the limitations of existing frameworks by offering a comprehensive evaluation of the dual-defense approach, thereby enhancing theoretical understanding and practical applications in AI resilience.

The study is technically feasible, relying on publicly available datasets and GPU resources, and aims to bridge the gap in existing literature regarding the generalizability of defense mechanisms. The research question posits how the integration of the proposed defenses enhances CNN robustness compared to standard architectures. Key limitations include potential generalizability issues and the risk of overfitting, which will be mitigated through extensive evaluations across diverse datasets and careful monitoring of confounding variables.

rubric_scores.level: 9-11: understandable but partially broad or insufficiently operationalized
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal identifies a relevant research problem regarding the robustness of CNNs against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. However, the operational definitions of key concepts like 'robustness' and 'dual-defense framework' are somewhat vague, lacking specificity in how these constructs will be measured and evaluated. Major weaknesses: Key concepts are not clearly operationalized, and the research boundaries are not well defined, making it difficult to ascertain the scope of the study. Next band requirements: To move into the next band, the proposal should provide precise operational definitions for all key constructs and clearly delineate the research boundaries.

rubric_scores.level: 9-11: generally connected but some weak transitions or unsupported assumptions
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal outlines a logical progression from problem identification to hypothesis formulation. However, the causal claims linking anomaly detection and frequency domain analysis to improved robustness are not sufficiently supported by empirical evidence. Major weaknesses: Weak transitions between the theoretical framework and the proposed methodology; assumptions regarding the effectiveness of the dual-defense framework are not scientifically justified. Next band requirements: Strengthening the causal claims with empirical evidence from existing literature and providing clearer connections between each stage of reasoning would improve coherence.

While the proposal attempts to introduce a dual-defense framework, it largely combines existing methods without sufficiently demonstrating how this integration offers a novel theoretical or methodological contribution. Major weaknesses: Lacks a clear articulation of how the proposed framework differs from existing literature, leading to questions about its originality. Next band requirements: To achieve a higher score, the proposal must clearly define the unique contributions of the dual-defense framework and how it advances understanding in the field.

The methodology is generally sound, with a clear plan for ablation studies and benchmark evaluations. However, it lacks detailed descriptions of the evaluation metrics and potential confounding factors. Major weaknesses: Insufficient detail on how confounding variables will be controlled and how the evaluation metrics will be operationalized. Next band requirements: Providing a more comprehensive methodology with explicit details on evaluation metrics and controls would enhance feasibility.

rubric_scores.level: 9-11: relevant literature used but somewhat surface-level
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal references relevant literature but does not engage deeply with it or critically analyze existing gaps, leading to a superficial understanding of the research context. Major weaknesses: Lacks critical synthesis of the literature and fails to identify unresolved tensions or contradictions in existing research. Next band requirements: A more thorough engagement with the literature, including a critical analysis of existing gaps and positioning relative to competing approaches, is needed.

rubric_scores.level: 5-6: strong master-level but limited theoretical depth
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal demonstrates some theoretical understanding but lacks depth in discussing the mechanisms underlying the proposed framework and its broader implications. Major weaknesses: Limited discussion of trade-offs, limitations, and failure cases, which are crucial for PhD-level research. Next band requirements: Incorporating a more sophisticated theoretical discussion and addressing potential limitations and failure cases would enhance academic depth.

The proposal is generally well-structured and clear, but some sections could benefit from improved conciseness and precision. Major weaknesses: Occasional repetition and lack of clarity in terminology detract from overall readability. Next band requirements: Refining the language for clarity and conciseness would improve the presentation quality.

evaluation.comments: Total score: 67.0/100. Academic level: Master's-level. Major strengths: Identifies a relevant and timely research problem.; Proposes a structured methodology with plans for ablation studies. Major weaknesses: Vague operational definitions of key concepts.; Insufficient theoretical grounding and novelty.; Lack of depth in literature engagement and academic discussion. Required improvements for true PhD-level quality: Provide clearer operational definitions and research boundaries.; Strengthen theoretical underpinnings and causal claims.; Engage more deeply with the literature and articulate unique contributions. Final verdict: The proposal demonstrates potential but lacks the rigor and depth expected of genuine PhD-level research maturity.
